How the interview runs (sourced)

The Coinbase SQL interview, as candidates report it

Coinbase does not publish the format. Each row is what candidates and prep guides have described publicly, with its source; where sources disagree, the row says so. Formats change — treat every specific as reported, not official.

Roles where SQL is testedData Science, Analytics and Data Engineering.[5]
Overall processA prep guide describes a 30-minute recruiter screen, a 30-minute online assessment for all candidates, a final round of four 60-minute interviews over Google Meet, then a work trial — a case on a dataset, presented to a panel.[1]
The SQL roundOne senior data scientist report (interview March 2025) calls the SQL and data analysis round the most important: two questions written in CoderPad, on trades and sign-ups, with follow-ups on how retention should be defined.[2]
OnsiteAnother data scientist report (interview October 2025) describes an onsite with a case study, two SQL questions — the second in three parts — and a live Python round of exploratory analysis and modelling on a dataset.[3]
Where sources differThe guide describes the data science round as a conversation plus a whiteboard part; the March 2025 report names CoderPad. Neither report says whether the SQL was run. A second guide lists more rounds, including an AI-led behavioural screen for some 2025–2026 candidates.[1][2][4]

The SQL that comes up

What Coinbase SQL questions test

Reported most often, in order

  • 1Time-window filters (the last 30 days)
  • 2COUNT DISTINCT and choosing the denominator
  • 3Retention and cohort timing (7-day retention)
  • 4Rates (adoption, transaction rate)
  • 5Time between events (adoption to first transaction)
  • 6First event per user, compared with later rows
  • 7Running and cumulative sums
  • 8Layered CTEs and window functions

Difficulty: Reported as medium by one candidate and hard by another; the medium report says the SQL itself was not especially hard and the interviewer weighed the reasoning. The data is crypto trades (user, asset, volume, time), sign-ups and first trades, and user transactions with an adoption time and a region.

Sample questions

Coinbase SQL question shapes, and where to practise them

Shapes candidates and guides report (paraphrased)

  • Trades by user, time, volume and asset: the share of users with three or more trades in the last 30 days.[2]
  • Users with a sign-up date and their trades: 7-day retention — and whether day zero is the sign-up or the first trade.[2]
  • User transactions with an adoption time and regions: adoption and transaction rates, the time from adoption to first transaction, and transactions made outside the region of the user's first one.[3]
  • Trades by currency and day: daily volume per currency and the change from the day before.[5]

Every challenge in the Coinbase set, by topic

These are SQL Quest challenges matched to the topics candidates report for Coinbase — not questions Coinbase has asked.

Every query here runs on SQLite in your browser. Joins, GROUP BY, CTEs and window functions are written the same way in PostgreSQL, MySQL and Snowflake; dates are where they differ (SQLite's strftime('%Y-%m', ts) is to_char(ts, 'YYYY-MM') in PostgreSQL), and the app lists each difference beside every challenge.

Drill the skills the Coinbase set leans on, one at a time: GROUP BY exercises · Window function practice · Date function practice · CTE practice · JOIN practice — or browse every SQL practice question.
